decisions.reason: False positive: the Definition explicitly returns budget-exhausted at k=N and separates the exact extended recurrence from finite actual runs. The title describes a finite procedure with a discrepancy test, not an unconditional crossing theorem. At each admissible current state the positive shifted normal operator is invertible under Countable Choice; domain/evaluation/solve failures have explicit outputs. The owning page and convergence theorem preserve the cap and exact-call caveats.

Confirmed nonfatal operational omission: initialization of k and the return to the stopping tests were only implicit in “At iteration k” and “next call”. Added k=0, explicit output tuples, and k←k+1 followed by repetition. The unchanged positive-shift equation has a unique solution; discrepancy precedes the cap at each state, and a new state outside U returns domain-failure on the next check.

Confirmed fatal unsupported inference (logic): F1 asserted projected minimization although the algorithm only prescribes rotations and back substitution; old step 3.1 did not show that its computed z was the minimizer. Replaced F1 with the actual instructions and proved QB_k=(R_k;0), Q beta_1 e_1=(d_k;eta_k), and residual squared = ||d_k-R_k z||^2+|eta_k|^2. Back substitution zeros the first term. Orthonormal Golub–Kahan bases transfer this minimum to the true residual, and the nonzero three-term forward coefficients identify the Krylov span. The Statement is unchanged, including k=0 and the nonbreakdown hypotheses.

Confirmed nonfatal citation/interface ambiguity: a full anchored run requires x0 in U, whereas this lemma only needs an algebraic anchor in X. Preserved its Statement and defined the standalone correction explicitly in F1. Step 1.2 now obtains its positive-shift inverse from the filter supplier applied to A_x and derives the identity by adding the current error equation. Neither F(x0) nor a run initialized at x0 is used. The continuous segment integral bounds t by 2kappa||Ae||; adjoint expansion yields H and z, and the two source filters give precisely the displayed residual/error bounds without requiring x_+ in B.

Confirmed fatal dependency-citation defect: F3 asserted compactness for every finite-rank Hilbert-space operator, omitting the supplier’s bounded-linear hypothesis. A finite-rank algebraic linear map need not be bounded. Corrected F3 to the exact bounded finite-dimensional-range result. Step 1.1 now proves ||A_N x||^2≤||x||^2/4 and identifies the explicit ordered range basis before invoking compactness; it also establishes boundedness of A before the norm-limit theorem. The noise norm, coordinate residual formula, finite-tail convergence, and Bernoulli lower bound at k_j=4^j remain valid.
